question: Will Ekrem İmamoğlu be convicted of a crime during Q4 2026?

calls.reasoning: Not yet resolved: last conviction was 11 Sep 2026 (Yazıcı insult case), outside the window. Main driver: CHP 38th convention criminal case (Ankara 26th Criminal Court of First Instance), where the prosecutor gave a final opinion on 21 Oct 2026 asking for 1-3 years for İmamoğlu. Defence responses are due at the 11 Nov hearing, so a verdict in Q4 is plausible and Turkish courts usually follow the prosecution in his cases. Extra chances: expert-witness case 8 Dec, espionage 23 Dec, diploma forgery 25 Dec. Risks: postponement, acquittal (he has been acquitted before), or a deferred verdict (HAGB) that may not count as a conviction. Market check: only Polymarket's 'released from custody in 2026?' at Yes 0.05 (~$6.8k volume); not a conviction contract, used only as evidence he stays jailed.

- Event window: 2026-10-01 -> 2026-12-31 per the criteria; as of 2026-11-03 about 34% has elapsed. No conviction dated in the window found as of 3 Nov.
- 11 Sep 2026: sentenced to 2 yrs 1 mo plus political ban in the Şadi Yazıcı insult retrial (outside the window). He had been acquitted twice before in that case (Turkish Minute, 11 Sep 2026).
- 16 Jul 2025: convicted in the Akın Gürlek threat/harassment case; Dec 2022: convicted in the YSK 'fools' case (upheld on appeal Sep 2025, now at the Court of Cassation). Acquitted in the Beylikdüzü tender case Oct 2025 (tr.wikipedia list of his cases).
- CHP 38th convention criminal case, Ankara 26th Criminal Court of First Instance: on 21 Oct 2026 the prosecutor's final opinion asked 1-3 yrs for 9 defendants including İmamoğlu (Political Parties Law Art. 112, 'fraud in voting') and acquittal for 3. Next hearing 11 Nov 2026; defence given until then to respond (Cumhuriyet/Saraymedya, Oct 2026). One summary said no verdict is expected on 11 Nov, but this may be the writer's inference.
- Expert-witness case: the earlier prosecutor said the 'influencing an expert' charge did not occur; Jul 2026 a new prosecutor asked for more time and the hearing moved to 8 Dec 2026. BirGün headline: the case had been 'expected to be dropped'.
- Diploma forgery case (Istanbul 59th Criminal Court of First Instance): on 6 Jul 2026 adjourned to 25 Dec 2026 to wait for the administrative diploma ruling to become final (the judge said the Council of State will take long). Sentence sought: 2.5-8.75 yrs.
- Espionage case: detention continued 29 Sep 2026, adjourned to 23 Dec 2026; 15-20 yrs sought.
- Official-car (makam aracı) case: 23 Oct 2026 the court ordered a 3-person expert report and adjourned to 12 Feb 2027 (outside the window).
- Istanbul municipality corruption mega-trial (400+ defendants): İmamoğlu began his defence 12 Oct 2026; a verdict is likely far off.
- Status quo: he stays jailed and most hearings end in adjournment. Over 2025-2026 he had about one first-instance conviction every 6-12 months (Jul 2025, Sep 2026).
- Searched but not found: any statement that a verdict is scheduled for 11 Nov; whether the defendants asked for or would get a deferred verdict (HAGB); any new final prosecution opinion in the expert-witness case.

calls.reasoning: No Q4 conviction yet as of Nov 3. Main path is the CHP 38th convention criminal case: the prosecutor's final opinion on Oct 21 sought 1-3 yrs; the defence responds Nov 11, a stage where verdicts often follow at that or the next hearing. P(verdict by Dec 31) ~0.68 given repeated postponements; P(conviction | verdict) ~0.8 given the courts' record in his political cases and that he would likely refuse a deferred verdict (HAGB). Other Dec hearings (expert-witness, espionage, diploma) add ~0.04. Polymarket custody-release 5% is a different contract; it only confirms the status quo.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: no Q4 conviction yet, the CHP convention case's final opinion on Oct 21, Nov 11 set for defence replies, and the other Dec hearings unlikely to yield convictions. The factual dispute over whether Nov 11 is a verdict session (Bianet says not anticipated, a haberler summary says expected) can't be settled without web access, so I treat it as roughly even and add a second chance at a December hearing. Whether HAGB counts is a judgment call; it needs consent, so it's a low-probability path. Combined: about 0.68 x 0.8 + 0.04 = ~0.59.
